EO6871.summary: Retain blocked disposition: older mission performance is established, but this order launches further investigations, appointments and reports whose performance is not established.
EO6871.scope_check: Operative lead adopts completed report; paragraph 1 expressly revokes EO6861 paragraph 1; paragraph 2 creates a fresh stay through December 1; paragraph 3 continues named committee for sheep/leather protests and November 15 report; paragraph 4 directs a NEW three-person committee for prison labor/sheltered workshops/Prison Labor Compact report by December 1; paragraph 5 directs Board report about Code exceptions/exemptions by January 15, 1935; paragraph 6 reserves further orders. These future reports are not proved by the recital describing the earlier October 10 report.
EO6871.earlier_end_check: June 14, 1935 is the supported repeal event for code approval/prescription/enforcement powers, not a proven universal first cessation. Schechter's section 3 delegation holding cannot be dismissed because this particular order was not cancelled by name. The October 21 unnamed-instrument constraint and October 28 evidence rule remain unreconciled with any categorical first-end shortcut. June 16, 1935 was replaced as the scheduled Title I expiry; April 1, 1936 is a conditional outer statutory limit, not this member's demonstrated first end. Paragraph 2 states a fixed inclusive December 1 stay and full force thereafter; that is a supported scheduled endpoint, subject to earlier/further orders, not a whole-order end. November 15, December 1 (paragraph 4) and January 15 are report deadlines only. The old committee's October 10 completed mission cannot end the new missions.
EO6871.independent_command_check: Paragraph 3 continues an existing institution and assigns new work. Paragraph 4 separately requires appointment and study extending to a Prison Labor Compact and competition with sheltered workshops. Paragraph 5 concerns Board reporting on prior grants of exemptions. These actor/subject differences require actual performance and authority tracing; their relation to a code does not decide all survival questions.
EO6871.savings_check: Distinguish completed performance and surviving records/institutions from prospective code enforcement. NIRA section 5 and S.J. Res. 113's proviso do not establish universal surviving liabilities, universal agreement conversion, or continuation of every administrative direction. No general savings-law source has been established in this application. The status and scope of any accrued rights/liabilities remain qualified.

source.quote: Now, Therefore, by virtue of and pursuant to the authority vested in me by Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act of June 16, 1933 (ch. 90, 48 Stat. 195), and in order to effectuate the purposes of said title and of my said Executive Order No. 6861, dated September 28, 1934, I, FRANKLIN D. ROOSEVELT, President of the United States, do hereby approve and adopt the report and recommendations of said committee and do order:

operative_clause_analysis.finding: Self-executing adoption of already completed report; no proof of later reports.

source.quote: 1. That paragraph numbered 1 of Executive Order No. 6861, dated September 28, 1934, be and it is hereby revoked.

operative_clause_analysis.finding: Express partial revocation, not all of EO6861.

source.quote: 2. That the effective date of said amendments to Articles III and IV of said Code be stayed to and including December 1, 1934, after which date said amendments shall be in full force and effect.

operative_clause_analysis.finding: Fresh fixed stay through December 1 inclusive; earlier changes remain to be searched.

source.quote: 3. That the committee heretofore appointed and constituted by the National Industrial Recovery Board, consisting of Willard E. Hotchkiss, Chairman, W. Jett Lauck, and Donald M. Nelson, be continued, with instructions further to investigate the protests of the Sheep Lined and Leather Garment Subdivision of the Cotton Garment Industry and report its findings and recommendations therein on or before November 15, 1934.

operative_clause_analysis.finding: Continue named committee with further investigation/report.

source.quote: 4. That the National Industrial Recovery Board forthwith appoint a committee of three impartial persons, which committee shall investigate the effects of competition between the products of prison labor and sheltered workshops on the one hand and of the cotton garment industry on the other, study the operation of the Prison Labor Compact especially as to the enforcement of the standards of competition with private industry established therein, and report to the National Industrial Recovery Board concerning said matters not later than December 1, 1934.

operative_clause_analysis.finding: New committee appointment and broader prison/workshop/Compact study.

source.quote: 5. That on or before January 15, 1935, the National Industrial Recovery Board report to me as to exceptions to and exemptions from the Code of Fair Competition for the Cotton Garment Industry, as amended, which may have been granted under the provisions of Article XV of said Code as amended.

operative_clause_analysis.finding: Separate Board report on exemptions by January 15.

source.quote: 6. That this Order shall be subject to my further orders in the premises.

operative_clause_analysis.finding: Reservation of later orders; not a cessation date.

comparators: 6861's affirmative performance recital does not prove performance of 6871's newly assigned duties.
unresolved_material_gaps: Further sheep/leather report, new prison-labor committee appointment/report and exemptions report performance unknown.
Prison Labor Compact text and its authority not read; independent reach cannot be assumed or excluded.
Further orders affecting stay or committees and actual administrative transfer/cessation unresolved.

correction_route.destination: current native packet producer; independent review before any filing
required_steps: Seek each report and receipt separately, plus new committee appointment records and Compact authority.
Keep prior October 10 report/adoption and old-stay revocation as established events; distinguish new December stay and new missions.
Review 7075/7076/7252 applicability individually without assigning their dates as automatic endings.

No new raw-page authentication; APP number/date metadata and attached reports not independently certified here.
No complete code text or full administrative archive searched; no exhaustive absence assertion.
Exact resulting claims require new independent source review and ordinary controls. Shared review approves only conditional propositions.
